meta.titre: Food Preservation in the Kitchen: Why Food Decays and Methods That Slow It Down
meta.sous_theme: Causes of food spoilage, principles and methods of preservation

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In the mango season a market is full of fruit at very low prices, and by the end of the week much of it has rotted. A woman who dries, cooks with sugar or smokes the surplus can sell it months later. Fish and tomatoes spoil in a day or two in the heat unless they are treated. The GCE asks why food spoils, how each preservation method works, and often asks for a fixed number of ways of slowing down decay.

items: Micro-organisms such as bacteria, yeasts and moulds are living things too small to see.
Micro-organisms need food, moisture and warmth to grow.

sections.titre: Why food spoils and how preservation works
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Causes of spoilage
1. **Micro-organisms**: bacteria, yeasts and moulds feed on the food and make it sour, slimy, smelly or mouldy. Fermentation is the action of yeast (and some bacteria) on sugars, producing alcohol and gas, or acids.
2. **Enzymes** in the food itself cause over-ripening and browning of cut fruit.
3. **Air and light** can change fats, making them rancid.

Micro-organisms grow best with **food, moisture, warmth and time**. Preservation takes away one of these conditions or destroys the micro-organisms.

### Methods of preservation
| Group | Methods | How they work |
|---|---|---|
| Heat | Pasteurising, sterilising, canning, bottling, boiling | Heat kills micro-organisms; the container is then sealed so that no new ones enter |
| Cold | Refrigerating, freezing | Low temperature slows (refrigerator) or stops (freezer) their growth |
| Removing water | Sun drying, smoking, dehydrating | Without moisture they cannot grow; smoking also deposits substances from the smoke |
| Salt, sugar and acid | Salting fish and meat, jam, pickling in vinegar | Salt and sugar draw water out of the food and micro-organisms; vinegar makes conditions too acid |
| Excluding air | Airtight containers, covering food | Stops contamination |
| Preservatives | Approved chemicals | Added in small amounts; see the label |

### Ways of slowing down decay
Keep food cold, keep it dry, cover it and store it in clean airtight containers, cook it properly and eat it soon, keep the kitchen clean, buy fresh food, use the oldest food first, and use salt, sugar, vinegar, smoke or drying where suitable. Signs of spoilage: bad smell, slime, mould, change of colour or taste, and a bulging can.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to pick the heat preservative methods from a list.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Heat methods are those in which the food is heated to kill micro-organisms: pasteurising, sterilising, canning and bottling. Drying, salting, smoking, freezing and adding sugar or vinegar are not heat methods. Blanching vegetables in boiling water before freezing is a short heat treatment that destroys enzymes.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how sugar, salt or acid preserve food.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A strong sugar or salt solution draws water out of the food and out of any micro-organism that lands on it. The water is no longer available, so they cannot grow. Fruit is boiled with sugar for jam; the hot jam is poured into clean jars and sealed. In pickling the food is stored in vinegar, whose acid slows the growth of micro-organisms. Always use clean jars and cover them.

sections.enonce_markdown: Outline four ways in which a household can slow down the decay of fresh tomatoes bought in bulk. (8 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Outline" asks for four short points, and 8 marks for four points means 2 marks for each, so each point needs a short reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Four ways, each with a few words of explanation.

etapes.justification: Every way of slowing decay removes or reduces food, moisture, warmth or entry of micro-organisms.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Remove warmth, remove moisture, or exclude germs.

etapes.justification: Different methods earn separate marks; do not repeat "keep cold" twice.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Cool storage, sorting, drying, cooking and bottling.

etapes.action: Write each method with its reason.
etapes.justification: The reason shows that you understand the principle.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Keep in a cool place or refrigerator, because low temperature slows the growth of micro-organisms. 2. Remove bruised or rotting tomatoes, because decay spreads to the others. 3. Cook into a sauce and bottle it in clean sealed jars, because heat kills germs and the seal keeps them out. 4. Dry in thin slices in the sun, because without moisture micro-organisms cannot grow.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Tomatoes keep longer if they are kept cool, sorted so that spoiled ones are removed, cooked and bottled in sealed jars, or dried in thin slices, because each method lowers the temperature, removes moisture or kills or shuts out micro-organisms.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that freezing food kills all the bacteria in it.
items.pourquoi_faux: Freezing makes micro-organisms inactive but does not kill them.
items.correction_markdown: Say that freezing stops their growth; thawed food must be cooked and eaten soon.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing "drying" and "sun drying" as two different methods in a list of five.
items.pourquoi_faux: They are the same idea, so only one mark can be given.
items.correction_markdown: Give five different ways: for example keep cold, keep dry, cover food, add salt or sugar, and smoke it.

items.erreur_markdown: Including drying, salting or freezing among heat preservation methods.
items.pourquoi_faux: A heat method needs heat to kill micro-organisms.
items.correction_markdown: Heat methods: pasteurising, sterilising, canning and bottling.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that fermentation is caused by parasites.
items.pourquoi_faux: Parasites live on or in a host and do not ferment food. Fermentation is brought about by micro-organisms such as yeast and some bacteria.
items.correction_markdown: Fermentation is the breakdown of sugars by yeast (or bacteria) into products such as alcohol and gas, or acids.

items.erreur_markdown: Eating food from a bulging can because the date is still valid.
items.pourquoi_faux: A swollen can may hold gas made by growing bacteria.
items.correction_markdown: Throw it away without tasting it.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Name three micro-organisms that spoil food. (b) State two conditions that micro-organisms need for fast growth. (c) Name two heat preservation methods. (d) Name the process by which sugars are broken down by yeast.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Bacteria, yeasts and moulds**. (b) Any two of **food, moisture, warmth, time**. (c) Any two of **pasteurising, sterilising, canning, bottling**. (d) **Fermentation**.

items.enonce_markdown: A woman makes mango jam from 4 kg of mangoes at $400$ FCFA per kg and 3 kg of sugar at $700$ FCFA per kg. Firewood costs $500$ FCFA and she uses 12 jars at $150$ FCFA each (assumed prices). (a) Find the total cost. (b) Find the cost for each jar if she fills all the jars. (c) She sells each jar for $800$ FCFA. Find her profit on all the jars. (d) State two things that she must do to keep the jam safe.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Mangoes: $4 \times 400 = 1\,600$. Sugar: $3 \times 700 = 2\,100$. Jars: $12 \times 150 = 1\,800$. Total: $1\,600 + 2\,100 + 500 + 1\,800 = 6\,000$, so **$6\,000$ FCFA**. (b) $6\,000 \div 12 = 500$, so **$500$ FCFA** a jar. (c) Profit per jar: $800 - 500 = 300$. For 12 jars: $300 \times 12 = 3\,600$, so **$3\,600$ FCFA**. (d) Any two of: use clean jars; seal the jars while the jam is hot or close them tightly; store in a cool dry place; use enough sugar; discard jam that grows mould.

items.enonce_markdown: A fish seller has 10 kg of fresh fish bought at $1\,500$ FCFA per kg and cannot sell it all before it spoils. She decides to smoke it. (a) Find what the fish cost her. (b) Explain two ways in which smoking helps to preserve the fish. (c) After smoking she has 6 kg of dried fish, which she sells at $2\,800$ FCFA per kg. Find her income and say whether it covers the cost of the fish. (d) State two precautions for storing the smoked fish.
items.solution_markdown: (a) $10 \times 1\,500 = 15\,000$, so **$15\,000$ FCFA**. (b) Heat and smoke dry the fish, and without moisture micro-organisms cannot grow; substances from the smoke also help to slow down the growth of micro-organisms. (c) $6 \times 2\,800 = 16\,800$, so **$16\,800$ FCFA**. This is more than $15\,000$ FCFA, so it **does** cover the cost of the fish, with $16\,800 - 15\,000 = 1\,800$, that is $1\,800$ FCFA, left over (before other costs such as fuel and wood). (d) Any two of: make sure that the fish is completely dry; store in a dry, airtight, covered container; keep away from insects and rats; keep in a cool place; check for mould.

items_markdown: Food spoils through micro-organisms (bacteria, yeasts, moulds), enzymes, and the action of air on fats.
Micro-organisms need food, moisture, warmth and time; preservation removes one of these or kills them.
Heat methods: pasteurising, sterilising, canning, bottling. Cold: refrigerating, freezing. Others: drying, smoking, salting, sugar, vinegar.
Fermentation is the breakdown of sugars by yeast (and some bacteria) into products such as alcohol, gas or acids.
For "ways of slowing down decay" give the exact number of different points, each with a short reason.
Throw away food from a bulging can and food that smells, is slimy or is mouldy.
